final_proof:
Let $x = \tuple{x_1, \dots, x_n}$ and $y = \tuple{y_1, \dots, y_n}$ be ordered tuples of real numbers, and let $\alpha = \tuple{\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n}$ be a multiindex.

By the definition of multiindex operations, we have:
$$ (x + y)^\alpha = \prod_{j=1}^n (x_j + y_j)^{\alpha_j} $$

Since each $x_j, y_j$ are real numbers and $\alpha_j$ is a non-negative integer, we apply the standard Binomial Theorem to each factor $(x_j + y_j)^{\alpha_j}$:
$$ (x_j + y_j)^{\alpha_j} = \sum_{\beta_j = 0}^{\alpha_j} \dbinom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j} x_j^{\beta_j} y_j^{\alpha_j - \beta_j} $$

Substituting this back into the product yields:
$$ (x + y)^\alpha = \prod_{j=1}^n \left( \sum_{\beta_j = 0}^{\alpha_j} \dbinom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j} x_j^{\beta_j} y_j^{\alpha_j - \beta_j} \right) $$

By the distributive property of multiplication over addition, we expand this finite product of sums into a multiple sum over all possible combinations of indices $\beta_j$:
$$ (x + y)^\alpha = \sum_{\beta_1 = 0}^{\alpha_1} \dots \sum_{\beta_n = 0}^{\alpha_n} \prod_{j=1}^n \left( \dbinom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j} x_j^{\beta_j} y_j^{\alpha_j - \beta_j} \right) $$

We can rearrange the terms inside the product:
$$ (x + y)^\alpha = \sum_{\beta_1 = 0}^{\alpha_1} \dots \sum_{\beta_n = 0}^{\alpha_n} \left( \prod_{j=1}^n \dbinom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j} \right) \left( \prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{\beta_j} \right) \left( \prod_{j=1}^n y_j^{\alpha_j - \beta_j} \right) $$

Let $\beta = \tuple{\beta_1, \dots, \beta_n}$ be a multiindex. The multiple sum over $0 \le \beta_j \le \alpha_j$ for each $j = 1, \dots, n$ is exactly equivalent to a single sum over the multiindex inequality $0 \le \beta \le \alpha$.

By the definition of the multiindex binomial coefficient and multiindex powers, we have the identities:
$$ \prod_{j=1}^n \dbinom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j} = \dbinom{\alpha}{\beta} $$
$$ \prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{\beta_j} = x^\beta $$
$$ \prod_{j=1}^n y_j^{\alpha_j - \beta_j} = y^{\alpha - \beta} $$

Substituting these multiindex definitions into our expansion yields the desired result:
$$ (x + y)^\alpha = \sum_{0 \le \beta \le \alpha} \dbinom{\alpha}{\beta} x^\beta y^{\alpha - \beta} $$

This completes the proof.
